subject: CPRA addendum: confirmation of service provider role and onshore fallback plan
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@blueharbor.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Jensen <cjensen@blueharbor.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: CPRA addendum questions: classification + onshore fallback

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. Before we circulate the CPRA addendum internally I need two clarifications for our legal and engineering teams so we can proceed with the pilot:

1) Classification: BlueHarbor needs confirmation in writing that Redwood is acting as a Service Provider (i.e., not an operator) for the telemetry/logging and inference result storage outlined in the DPA. We saw the earlier language but legal wants explicit wording covering cached prompts, diagnostics, and aggregated telemetry.

2) Onshore fallback: we require an onshore fallback plan for telemetry processing when offshore subprocessors are unavailable or during incident response. Can you point us to the operational doc or provide a short summary of how Redwood routes or reroutes telemetry to onshore subprocessors, and whether that path is guaranteed in the addendum? We also need timing (RTO) and any limits on the data types that will be routed.

If you can attach the current subprocessors list and a brief onshore-fallback playbook that would be helpful.

Appreciate a quick turnaround—our InfoSec review is on Tuesday next week.

Best,
Maria
Director, Vendor Security
BlueHarbor Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum questions: classification + onshore fallback

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list.

Short answers up front:
- Classification: Redwood confirms we process telemetry and inference outputs strictly as a Service Provider under CPRA/CPPA definitions. We do not control the purposes for which BlueHarbor uses inference outputs; we act per your instructions and the DPA. We will provide a short statement you can insert into the addendum if helpful.
- Onshore fallback: Redwood operates an onshore fallback capability for telemetry routing and emergency processing. I am attaching a lightweight playbook with execution steps, typical RTO targets, and the list of onshore fallback subprocessors we would use. For the addendum we can reference the playbook and include a commitment to route telemetry to onshore subprocessors where technically feasible; we typically prioritize encrypted prefix/KV cache purge and kinetic rerouting within 4–8 hours depending on region and data volume.

I’m looping in Kimberly (legal) for the precise contract language and Karthik (infra) for the technical caveats.

Next steps: Kimberly can propose the redline language; Karthik can confirm any limits on specific telemetry categories (e.g., raw audio vs aggregated metrics). Once you have the redline we’ll route to our privacy team for sign-off.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CPRA addendum questions: classification + onshore fallback

Maria — attaching two items per Sofia’s note:
- subprocessors_list_202606.pdf (current visible subprocessors with residency and roles)
- onshore_fallback_playbook_v2.docx (high-level runbook with stages, RTO ranges, and responsibilities)

Suggested contract snippet you can use in the addendum (feel free to copy/paste):

"Redwood Inference acts as a Service Provider with respect to Customer Data as defined under the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA). Redwood processes Customer Data only at Customer's direction and does not independently determine the purposes or means of processing. Redwood will not sell, retain, use, or disclose Customer Data other than as necessary to provide the Services under the DPA and this Addendum."

Suggested onshore fallback clause for the addendum:

"In the event of offshore subprocessors becoming unavailable or where Customer requires onshore processing for regulatory/incident purposes, Redwood will, subject to technical feasibility and prior notice where practicable, route telemetry and processing to onshore subprocessors identified in Redwood's subprocessors list. Redwood's targeted recovery time objective (RTO) for onshore rerouting is typically four to eight (4–8) hours for aggregated telemetry and thirty (30) to seventy-two (72) hours for complete forensic dataset rehydration, depending on data size and legal hold obligations. Certain high-volume raw data types (e.g., uncompressed audio streams) may require staged transfer and are excluded from the immediate RTO guarantees; such types will be handled per the playbook and documented exceptions."

A few notes and caveats:
- The RTO ranges above reflect operational targets and will be included in the addendum as "targeted" (not SLA-backed) unless Redwood and BlueHarbor agree to a paid SLA amendment.
- We cannot guarantee absolute zero offshore processing prior to rerouting; the clause includes an operational commitment to reroute upon trigger.
- For forensic transfers we may require a signed BAA/transfer order and coordination window to ensure data integrity.

Let us know if this language works; Maria, if you can send your redline I’ll review and we can mark up the addendum.

Kimberly — thanks, that’s helpful detail and the language reads well. I’ve attached a quick redline of the CPRA addendum showing where BlueHarbor would like the explicit service-provider sentence and the onshore fallback reference to live. A couple follow-ups: 

1) Can Redwood mark the onshore fallback paragraph as "targeted" as you suggested, but add a short sentence committing to provide a post-incident timeline and remediation summary within five (5) business days? That helps our compliance folks.
2) For the subprocessors list: do you have a separate, regularly updated hosted list (URL) we can reference so we don't have to reattach on every renewal? If so, we prefer a hosted canonical link with an attestation date.

I’ve attached: blueharbor_dpa_redline.pdf (our edits). If you can confirm the hosted subprocessors URL and accept the post-incident timeline language we can move this to procurement for signature.

Best,
Maria

Attachments: [attachment: blueharbor_dpa_redline.pdf (PDF - 38KB)]

Subject: Re: CPRA addendum questions: classification + onshore fallback

Maria — thanks for the redline and the two asks. Agreed on both items:

1) We will add the post-incident timeline commitment: Redwood will provide a remediation and timeline summary within five (5) business days following an onshore fallback-triggering incident, subject to applicable legal constraints. We will keep the RTO language as "targeted" per Kimberly's note unless BlueHarbor requests and agrees to an SLA amendment.
2) Canonical subprocessors list: Redwood maintains a hosted, read-only subprocessors page with attestation dates. The canonical link is: https://status.redwood.com/subprocessors (each export includes an attestation header and timestamp). We will include that URL and the attestation reference in the addendum.

Next steps: Kimberly will incorporate your redline and our minor edits into a new PDF and circulate. Karthik will confirm the exclusion list for high-volume raw data types and provide a short paragraph to append to the playbook about transfer staging.

Once we have the agreed draft I can push the DocuSign link to your procurement contact; I’ve also attached a HubSpot deal id for reference in case you want to track it on your side (HubSpot deal: 6789012).

Thanks — Sofia
